title: GPU defragmentation + progressive CPU fallback with OOM fingerprinting and retry policy
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: We continue to see transient OOMs on high-concurrency hosted nodes when sustained continuous batching + KV growth causes GPU memory fragmentation and prevents allocator compaction. These OOMs disproportionately affect long-lived chat sessions and heavy embedding workloads. Current mitigations (aggressive eviction, model fallback) are reactive and cause user-visible errors or large latency spikes.
proposed_solution: 1) Implement an in-process GPU defragmentation shim that opportunistically triggers between batch windows to coalesce free memory (aligns with the serving runtime's kernel selection cadence). 2) Add an OOM fingerprinting layer that records allocator state, KV cache occupancy, recent batch sizes, and per-request sequence length at the time of OOM to the internal crash-telemetry stream. 3) Progressive fallback policy: when an OOM fingerprint is detected, attempt (a) non-blocking KV compaction + pin-down of active KV pages, (b) soft admission control (reduce incoming batch admission rate for 200ms), (c) fallback to a CPU-hosted distilled model for the affected session with transparent retry semantics and degraded-SLO flag. 4) Integrate the above into the request router with a 3-stage retry policy and circuit-breaker to avoid cascading CPU overload. 5) Add dashboarding and an incident runbook that maps OOM fingerprints to recommended config changes (batch_limit/kv_quota/static_model_swap).
acceptance_criteria:
- GPU defrag shim runs without increasing p99 latency by >5% on synthetic load.
- OOM fingerprint payloads appear in telemetry for 100% of OOM events in staging.
- Progressive fallback recovers 90% of previously-failing sessions within two retry attempts, with tail latency < 2x normal.
- No user-facing 500s introduced by fallback path during a 24h chaos experiment.
- Grafana panels added: OOM fingerprints per node, fallback events per model, CPU fallback latency, batch admission rate reduction events.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind runtime feature flag and tenant opt-in. 2) Canary on internal infra with 5% traffic for 48h. 3) Run synthetic workload ramp (ConversationLongTail, EmbeddingBurst) and compare baseline to canary. 4) If stable, increase to 25% for 72h and evaluate. 5) Global rollout with monitoring alerts and an automatic rollback if regressions tripped.
telemetry_and_alerting:
- Add OOM-fingerprint index to crash-telemetry (fields: allocator_snapshot_id, kv_occupancy_pct, recent_batch_histogram, seq_len_p95, model_variant).
- New alert: >5 OOM fingerprints of same family within 10m on a node => page on-call.
- SLO dashboard: CPU-fallback success rate and fallback-induced error rate.
risk_and_mitigation:
Risk: Defrag operations could momentarily increase GPU memory pressure or block scheduling. Mitigation: make defrag opportunistic and preemptible; run only in inter-batch idle windows and back off when seen p99 spike.
Risk: CPU fallback could overload host CPUs. Mitigation: circuit-breaker + per-tenant CPU fallback quota + telemetry to backfill capacity.
Risk: privacy/PII in telemetry. Mitigation: fingerprint payloads are hashed/aggregated; no raw prompt text is sent.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for defrag shim state machine and backoff.
- Integration test: synthetic generator that constructs kv growth patterns and repeated long-prefix requests to force fragmentation.
- Chaos experiment: run for 6h with fault injector to simulate transient memory pressure and verify no user 500s.
- Load test: compare p50/p95/p99 with and without defrag under representative traffic.
